title: Enchiridion (Epictetus)
author: Various
content:
English-language translations of Enchiridion include:
The Manuell of Epictetus, trans. by James Sandford (1567)
Epictetus his Manuall and Cebes his Table, trans. by John Healey (1610)
The Life and Philosophy of Epictetus, trans. by John Davies (1670)
Epicteti Enchiridion. The morals of Epictetus made English, in a poetical paraphrase, trans. by Ellis Walker (1692)
Epictetus his Morals, with Simplicius his Comment, trans. by George Stanhope (1694)
Epictetus his Morals: Done from the Original Greek, by a Doctor of Physick, trans. by Anonymous (1702)
The Porch and Academy Opened; Or, Epictetus's Manual Newly Turn'd Into Verse with Notes, trans. by "J. W." (1707)
The Enchiridion of Epictetus, trans. by Mary Wortley Montagu (1710). First published in her collected Works, vol. 1, (1803)
The Manual of Epictetus, the philosopher, translated by a "Person of Quality", published by William Bond (1730)
The Manual of Epictetus's Morals, trans. by Timothy Thomas (1743). Manuscript only.
The Enchiridion, or Manual, of Epictetus, trans. by Elizabeth Carter (1759)
The Meditations of Marcus Aurelius Antoninus, with the Manual of Epictetus trans. by Henry McCormac (1844) (transcription project)
The Enchiridion, trans. by Thomas Wentworth Higginson (1865)
Ancient Philosophy; Or the Enchiridion of Epictetus, and Chrusa Epe of Pythagoras, trans. by Thomas Talbot (1872) (transcription project)
The Encheiridion or Manual, translated by George Long (1877)
The Encheiridion of Epictetus, trans. by T. W. H. Rolleston (1881)
Manual of Epictetus, trans. by Percy Ewing Matheson (1916)
The Encheiridion, or Manual, translated by William Abbott Oldfather (1928)
